model: claude-cli:haiku (detection, 2 independent live runs) + claude-cli:haiku (judge, 4 calls: 1 fresh + 3x against a fixed saved transcript)
result: root-caused: real model-reasoning inconsistency, not judge flakiness or a prompt/harness bug
note: The harness doesn't persist raw responses, so the original transcript from the regression run above was gone, but the same underlying pattern reproduced immediately on a fresh run. Two independent live detection runs on the identical contract gave OPPOSITE conclusions about the same bug: Run A correctly traced that both balance reads happen into locals before either write, so the second write uses a stale value and the balance INCREASES (matches ground truth); Run B assumed the far more common sequential subtract-then-add self-transfer shape and concluded the operations cancel out, balance UNCHANGED (wrong for this contract's actual read-both-then-write-both ordering, though it would be the CORRECT analysis for a differently-ordered contract). Re-ran the judge 3x directly against Run B's own saved transcript: 3/3 NO_MATCH with specific, correct reasoning each time — the judge was not the flaky part, the underlying detection model's reasoning was. Honest conclusion: a real, characterizable capability gap (order-of-operations-subtle bugs in a small, simple contract) — a different shape than the earlier large-contract-capacity finding, and the existing complexity heuristic (lines/imports/functions) would never flag this 5-line function as needing escalation, so the existing model-escalation mechanism doesn't help here. Naming a new miss category accurately (order-dependent bugs uncorrelated with existing complexity signals) is the deliverable of this investigation, not a reason to escalate to a bigger model by default without evidence that would actually help broadly.

corpus: defivulnlabs_subset (self-transfer fixture, A/B on the prompt fix)
result: OLD prompt 3/6 match (50.0%, SEM 20.4pp); NEW prompt (+aliasing checklist item) 5/6 match (83.3%, SEM 15.2pp); diff +33.3pp, 95% CI [-16.6pp, +83.2pp] — covers zero
note: Grounded in enterprise-AI-agent research on reliability decomposition (structure/scaffolding contributes roughly 9x the improvement of a verification loop alone — try a cheap prompt fix before an expensive self-consistency sampling scheme) and on rigorous eval methodology (any 'improvement' claim needs a standard error and a paired confidence interval, not a single anecdotal re-run — 'Adding Error Bars to Evals' is the exact discipline followed here). Added a new checklist item to the always-on prompt layer: whether two logically-distinct operands can alias to the same storage slot, and whether all reads happen before all writes to it — directly targeting the exact mechanism of the reproduced miss above. 6 live trials per condition, holding everything else fixed: directionally strong improvement (50%→83%) but the 95% CI on the difference covers zero — NOT yet statistically significant at this sample size. A rough power analysis: ~27-28 trials per condition would be needed for 80% power at this observed effect size — not run (cost/time), an honest, named gap. Decision made anyway: keep the free structural fix (zero added cost per run, grounded in the real reproduced mechanism, zero downside if unproven) and let the growing regression baseline accumulate real evidence over time rather than manufacture dozens of trials synthetically.
